literal: Cada pack posee gate individual `REGULATORY_PACK_<CODE>=PASS`. La falta de texto licenciado, publicación definitiva o aprobación de un pack bloquea exclusivamente su selección, uso oficial y evidencia runtime dependiente. section: ### Fase 7 — Integrated Audit + Third Parties + Resilience + Privacy
literal: AuditTest puede cubrir múltiples Requirements sólo mediante links tipados. Si los Requirements pertenecen a FrameworkVersion distintas, toda agrupación adicional debe citar un RequirementCrosswalkMapping aprobado, efectivo y con relationship_type `equivalent | partially_equivalent | overlaps | supports`. Coincidencia de numeración HLS nunca basta. Cada Requirement conserva identity, applicability, RequirementAssessment, result_status, domain_conclusion y lineage independientes.
Una persona puede ocupar varios roles en un equipo pequeño, pero debe registrarse el sombrero usado en cada aprobación y respetar las segregaciones obligatorias.

Cuando la fuente no asigna un código distinto a cada obligación dentro de una unidad, el importador genera un `requirement_code` estable y determinístico desde `source_locator + statement ordinal`, conserva el locator original y exige revisión humana antes de publicar. Una nueva extracción no puede renumerar silenciosamente Requirements publicados.

IA es asistencia gobernada, no autoridad de negocio. El backend controla contexto, autorización, minimización de datos, provenance, auditoría y human oversight antes de consumir `ia2.tcdx.int`. Ninguna salida IA puede crear hechos, permisos, estados o decisiones vinculantes fuera de los contratos aprobados.

No se declara “READY”, “DONE”, “PRODUCTION READY” ni equivalente por avance porcentual. El cierre exige evidencia de todos los gates y capacidades dependientes. La autoridad final de release corresponde al QA/Release Owner y aprobadores humanos definidos, nunca a Codex.
Fuera de este cierre acotado aplica fail-closed y `CODEX_VARIATION_BUDGET=ZERO`. La revisión humana previa a commit sigue siendo el siguiente gate de integración.
El mapping no transfiere cumplimiento ni conclusión. Cada Requirement mantiene RequirementApplicability y RequirementAssessment independientes.

La revisión semántica pre-física permanece satisfecha. Este baseline maestro, una vez publicado con aprobación humana registrada en el repositorio, autoriza exclusivamente `PHYSICAL_MODEL_DESIGN=AUTHORIZED`; no equivale a `PASS_FOR_IMPLEMENTATION`, no autoriza migraciones y no autoriza desarrollo funcional.

section: ### MI6F — temporary credential disclosure and uncertain-result contract (2026-10-02)
literal: `UNCERTAIN_RESULT` means the backend cannot prove whether Keycloak completed a sensitive mutation before an interruption. It neither claims success nor failure, repeats the mutation, retrieves a prior plaintext, nor discloses one. The API returns the standard `application/problem+json` envelope with `code=TCDX.CONFLICT.RECOVERY_REQUIRED`, HTTP 409 and `retryable=false`; its safe message directs an authorized operator to reconcile or initiate a fresh approved recovery. Audit records an uncertain/recovery-required outcome, actor, target when known, operation, reason when required, correlation and idempotency reference without a credential. A replay of the same key may return proven safe metadata or this recovery error, never a second credential action.

The human architecture decision approves exactly one internal technical user attribute, `tcdx_provision_reconciliation_marker`, for `managedIdentityProvision`. Before the Keycloak user-create call, the GRC backend generates a fresh opaque value from its runtime CSPRNG with at least 128 bits of random entropy. The marker is independent of username, email, tenant, business/personal data, UserIdentity ID and the plaintext `Idempotency-Key`; it is not supplied by the client or derived from any of those inputs. It is nonsecret technical metadata, never a credential, external identity key, authenticator, tenant/RBAC fact or response field. Knowledge of it grants no access. It is never mapped into OIDC tokens, displayed in UI, reported as business data or made editable. The existing `ops_audit.idempotency_records` claim may retain this nonsecret in-progress cross-system reference in its existing `result_ref` metadata; it must be durable and bound to the approved actor/operation/key/fingerprint **before** the Keycloak call. This is not a second identity authority, new GRC marker store, table or column. If the implementation cannot durably bind and recover the same marker through the canonical idempotency mechanism, it must stop before invoking Keycloak; it must not generate a different marker on replay.

MI6 may use a separate confidential service-to-service Keycloak Admin API client in the managed realm with only proven permissions for create/read safe metadata, enable/disable, temporary credential reset, TOTP removal and logout. It cannot reuse `tcdx-grc` or receive unrestricted `realm-admin`, `manage-realm`, `manage-clients`, impersonation or global event-view authority. If Keycloak requires materially broader privilege, MI6 stops absent a human-approved, fully governed exception under rector 43 §5.4; MI6E records the specific conditional exception below. The client is not a GRC RBAC actor; every GRC command authorizes the human Platform actor **before** any Admin API call.

An authorized operator provisions a named person with an optional email field and a temporary, single-use initial credential. The human-approved delivery model is a **direct secure operator-to-person handoff** without mailbox. Keycloak forces password setup/change and TOTP enrollment; a real TOTP challenge then establishes acceptable proof. Provisioning alone grants no membership or role. The permanent password is chosen by the person and unknown to the operator. MI6 must document and verify the person's identification, bounded temporary lifetime, one-use handling and exact admin API/permission/audit mappings before that lifecycle is implemented; no email, ticket, Git, log, report or prompt carries a credential.

The human architecture/security authority approved the Keycloak 26.7.5 user `manage` capability **only as a technical capability exception** for a dedicated confidential Managed Identity service account. Keycloak checks the same `manage` capability for MI6-required enable/disable, TOTP credential removal and session logout as for user deletion and federated-identity changes. This does **not** expand GRC functional authority beyond the eight MI6A operation IDs and routes above, add a GRC Permission or authorize a ninth operation. The human MI6E-R decision names Andrés Barouh as exception owner in the capacity `RESPONSABLE_ARQUITECTURA_DESARROLLO_TCDX_GRC` and sets expiration to `2027-04-02`, satisfying rector 43 §5.4 together with the linked ADR's elimination plan. This closes the MI6E governance blocker, not any MI6D implementation gate.
